title: Retirement orchestration and embedded migration kits for model API parity
creator: Priya Malhotra
description:
Goal: deliver a graduated retirement path for legacy model API tags and behaviors with embedded, self-serve migration kits so customers can upgrade with minimal code changes. This ticket coordinates cross-functional launch tasks: release notes automation, in-console migration UX, SDK warnings, migration CLI, outbound comms cadence, and success metrics.

Scope: sunset of two legacy model tags (legacy-v1, legacy-v1-compat) that diverge from current runtime behavior. Provide: automated compatibility reports, per-customer migration suggestions, a migration CLI to rewrite affected calls, server-side compatibility shim for 8 weeks, and cross-team playbook for support + AE outreach. Not in scope: blocking runtime changes for dedicated/private customers without opt-in (separate EPIC).

Key outcomes: reduce manual SRs by 60% for migration requests, <2% customer breakage at cutover, documented step-by-step migration kits, and orchestration runbook for canary->global cutover.
acceptance_criteria: Migration CLI (redwood-migrate) available as prerelease with commands: analyze, rewrite, dry-run
In-console migration hub shows compatibility score and next-step buttons for affected workspaces
Automated release notes generation includes per-impact snippets for customers (SDK, REST, embeddings, chat) and integrates with GH release draft
Server-side compatibility shim enabled and monitored for 8-week overlap, with automated rollback hooks
Support runbook, AE outreach templates, and FAQ published in Confluence linked from console
rollout_phases: Phase 0 - Discovery & signals (completed): inventory of tag usage, 90-day traffic matrix, customer risk buckets
Phase 1 - Migration tooling & docs (current): publish redwood-migrate alpha, migration hub UX mockups, release-note templates
Phase 2 - Canary + support pilot (2 weeks): enable shim for 10% of traffic, partner with top 10 customers for guided migrations
Phase 3 - Gradual ramp (4 weeks): increase shim coverage while enabling migration hub prompts and outbound comms
Phase 4 - Cutover window (target): disable legacy tag writes for new requests, maintain read-compat shim for 4 weeks, then full removal
Phase 5 - Post-mortem & lessons (2 weeks): incident review, docs updates, and metrics publication
communication_plan: T-30 days: initial public notice via dashboard banner + email to admins with migration workbook and calendar of webinars
T-14 days: release notes with detailed per-language migration snippets and automated GH release draft assigned to SDK teams
T-7 days: reminder email + suggested migration timeline for customers in medium/high risk buckets
Canary start: Slack channel #pm-versioning-updates for real-time cross-functional alerts
Cutover day: targeted emails 1 hour before, 30m after, and summary 24h after; post to status.redwood.ai where appropriate
launch_checklist: Finalize redwood-migrate CLI alpha and publish Docker image
Ship migration hub frontend (feature flag) and link to docs
Automate release notes snippets via release-notes-bot for console and SDK repos
Create Support runbook with triage rubric and escalation matrix
Schedule three customer webinars and prepare AE outreach lists
Configure observability dashboards: migration-rate, shim-traffic, error-rate-by-customer, rollback-triggered
Create automated success emails for customers who complete migration flow
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Undiscovered edge-case behavior causing model output regressions. Mitigation: pilot with top 10 customers + gated canary and explicit fallback to legacy runtime for flagged customers.
Risk: High support volume at cutover. Mitigation: pre-bake FAQ, expand on-call rotation during cutover week, and prepare templated PRs for SDK teams.
Risk: Automation produces noisy false-positives for compatibility. Mitigation: human review queue for 'high-impact' rewrites and confidence threshold on analyzer before recommending rewrite.
Risk: Private/Dedicated customers need separate upgrade path. Mitigation: include targeted comms and operator-run migration package; defer forced cutover until opt-in confirmation for those tenants.
